components.name: Primary Filled Button — Light
components.description: The single primary action on a light surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-light { display: inline-flex; min-width: 48px; min-height: 50px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 24px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #A8580A; color: #FFFFFF; font: 700 15px/1 SpaceGrotesk, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.3px; transition: filter 160ms; } .ds-btn-light:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-light:active { filter: brightness(0.94); } .ds-btn-light:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(180, 104, 15, 0.45); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-icon { width: 20px; height: 20px; fill: currentColor; }

components.name: Pocket Player Mark — Light
components.description: The empty-state mark: a moulded housing with a blank recessed screen and a wheel whose centre key lights.
components.css: .ds-pocket-light { width: 250px; height: 280px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; } .ds-pocket-light::before { content: ""; position: absolute; } .ds-pocket-light { background: linear-gradient(#F8F3E6 0%, #EAE1CB 55%, #D6CBAF 100%); border: 1px solid #AD9F82; border-radius: 16px; width: 158px; padding: 22px 16px; gap: 24px; } .ds-pocket-light .ds-pocket-screen { display: block; width: 100%; height: 96px; background: #DCD4BD; border: 1px solid #D0C6AF; border-radius: 5px; } .ds-pocket-light .ds-pocket-wheel { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 108px; height: 108px; border-radius: 50%; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #F4EDDD, #E3DAC2 55%, #CFC4A8); border: 1px solid #AD9F82; } .ds-pocket-light .ds-pocket-key { width: 42px; height: 42px; border-radius: 50%; background: #A8580A; }

components.name: Click Wheel — Dark
components.description: The player transport: a painted moulded face with ordinary buttons laid over it, so every key keeps its tooltip, focus stop, 48px target, and semantics.
components.css: .ds-wheel { position: relative; width: 244px; height: 244px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid #14110C; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #443D2D, #302A20 55%, #241F18); } .ds-wheel::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 71px; border-radius: 50%; background: #211D16; border: 1px solid #14110C; } .ds-wheel-key { position: absolute; width: 48px; height: 48px; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: transparent; color: #B0A695; font-size: 18px; } .ds-wheel-key.ds-n { top: 12px; left: 98px; } .ds-wheel-key.ds-s { bottom: 12px; left: 98px; } .ds-wheel-key.ds-w { left: 12px; top: 98px; } .ds-wheel-key.ds-e { right: 12px; top: 98px; } .ds-wheel-centre { position: absolute; z-index: 1; left: 78px; top: 78px; width: 88px; height: 88px; border: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: #F0A93B; color: #2A1A00; font-size: 34px; } .ds-wheel-key:focus-visible, .ds-wheel-centre:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(240, 169, 59, 0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Readout — Dark

components.description: A menu row: a bezelled square cover, title and author, the resume counter in the readout face, and the arrow into it.

components.css: .ds-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; min-height: 80px; padding: 8px 16px; text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid #D0C6AF; background: #FCFAF4; color: #211E17; font-family: SpaceGrotesk, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-row-cover { flex: none; width: 56px; height: 56px; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: 5px; border: 1px solid #AD9F82; background: linear-gradient(#F8F3E6 0%, #EAE1CB 55%, #D6CBAF 100%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #E4DCC7; color: #3A3226; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-row-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; min-width: 0; flex: 1; } .ds-row-text strong { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-row-author { font-size: 14px; color: #63594A; } .ds-row-bar { display: block; height: 4px; border-radius: 2px; background: #CDC3AC; overflow: hidden; } .ds-row-bar i { display: block; height: 100%; background: #A8580A; } .ds-row-resume { color: #A8580A; font: 700 12px/1.35 SpaceMono, ui-monospace, Menlo, 'Courier New', monospace; } .ds-row-arrow { flex: none; color: #8A7F6B; font-size: 18px; }

narrative.overview:
The interface should feel like a well-made personal player from the early
2000s: a brushed housing, a screen recessed behind a bezel, printed keys on a
moulded wheel, and one amber that marks the row you are on. The product is the
same calm, offline listening room it always was; what changed is that the room
now has the shape of a device you could hold.

The visual language uses drawn bevels instead of blur, hairline rules instead
of cards, monospaced digits for anything that counts, and tight corners
everywhere. Material 3 roles still structure Android presentation, iOS
navigation and transitions retain familiar platform behavior, and macOS
restructures content for resizable pointer-and-keyboard windows. The period
belongs to the surfaces, the geometry, and the wheel — never to the behavior:
every control underneath is a stock platform control with its own tooltip,
focus, touch target, and semantics.
keyCharacteristics: Brushed chrome housing over a plain screen, in coordinated light and dark.
One amber for the primary action, the marked row, and the bar of progress.
Space Grotesk for reading, Space Mono for readouts; both bundled.
Bevelled hairline edges; tight 3-6 logical-pixel corners; no drop shadows.
Native navigation, controls, touch targets, and reduced-motion behavior.

rules.name: The One Amber Voice Rule
rules.text: Amber belongs to the primary action, the row being played, and the bar of progress; its rarity is what makes it legible.

rules.name: The Bevel, Not Blur Rule
rules.text: Depth is a dark hairline and a lit hairline, or a two-stop gradient across a moulded face. It is never a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Reading Rhythm Rule
rules.text: Preserve semantic type roles and text scaling; never shrink or tighten copy merely to force a preferred composition.

rules.name: The Digits Sit Still Rule
rules.text: A number that changes while you watch it is set in the readout face, so the line beside it never reflows.

rules.name: The Flat-Behind-the-Bevel Rule
rules.text: Separate layers with bevels, tonal roles, and spacing; do not add drop shadows to rows, housing bars, readouts, or controls.

dos: use semantic Material color roles so light and dark appearances remain coordinated.
reserve amber for the primary action, the marked row, and progress.
take the ink on the marked row from the palette rather than assuming white: the lit amber of dark appearance will not carry it.
set every counted quantity in the readout face.
keep content flows native, scrollable, safe-area aware, and resilient to text scaling.
draw period surfaces with bevels and gradients, and leave the control underneath a stock platform control.
disable the empty-state motion when reduced motion or accessible navigation is requested.
donts: add drop shadows, glass effects, or arbitrary accent colors.
paint a control that a real button could be laid over instead.
wrap empty states, settings groups, or list rows in generic cards.
replace platform navigation, back behavior, segmented controls, list tiles, sliders, or progress indicators with web-shaped imitations.
fabricate cover art, catalog content, a logo, or a final product name, and don't imitate the branding of any device the period recalls.
stretch centered reading content across tablet widths or compress it to preserve a fixed phone composition.
